body.statement: Determine whether a class-uniform constant \(C\) exists such that every aligned pair \(\theta,\widetilde\theta\in\mathcal M_{n,k,m}(c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0)\) obeys \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\theta,\widetilde\theta)\le C\mathcal E(\theta,\widetilde\theta)^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\). The primary kill test is \(n=2\), \(k=2\), \(m=1\): prove the normalized weighted inequality for arbitrary bounded divergence-free periodic \(C^2\) fields, or construct a legal joint-critical or oscillatory sequence with an unbounded normalized ratio and then test whether it integrates to a full-law counterexample.
body.justification: This is the genuinely open analytic content separating a publishable full-class frontier from a radial analogue.
body.gap: Friesecke--James--Müller control a matrix-well defect and Dacorogna--Moser control a prescribed determinant; neither controls a divergence-free map from Morse-degenerate scalar transport equations.
body.consumer: An affirmative answer closes the full nuisance-uniform modulus; a negative answer identifies the minimal spacing, profile, or decoder restriction required for valid causal recovery.

obligation.obstruction: The determinant residual controls only approximate incompressibility, while each scalar ratio loses coercivity on a critical line and its one-dimensional nuisance profile can absorb fiber means. No frozen hypothesis supplies the required joint weighted coercivity or an endpoint-regular volume correction.
obligation.attempted: The synthetic product law was used to retain determinant error, Hodge linearization was examined, and joint-critical, anisotropic, one-strip, and oscillatory Hamiltonian scalings were tested. Ratio-only strips fail because their determinant error is larger; isotropic radial packets attain the proposed exponent; anisotropic and oscillatory packets inspected here do not violate it. A Dacorogna--Moser or Hodge correction still lacks an endpoint \(C^k\) bound strong enough to close the nonlinear interpolation without an exponent or logarithmic loss.
obligation.partial_result: The full-law residual reduction is proved, a weaker compactness/interpolation route gives continuity but not the claimed sharp exponent, and Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:radial\text{-}subclass\text{-}frontier}\) proves the exact exponent on the infinite-dimensional radial subclass. The Hamiltonian family proves the matching lower bound on every full class containing it.
